questions.question: What is significant about the CMS-03 satellite launch by Indian Space Research Organisation in November 2025?

options.text: It is the heaviest communication satellite launched by India.
It is the first private payload launched from India.
It is the first navigation satellite mission from India.
It is India’s first Mars mission satellite.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is the heaviest communication satellite launched by India.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **CMS-03** is a state-of-the-art **communication satellite** designed and developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** to provide advanced telecommunication services.
 
• Scheduled for launch in **November 2025**, the **CMS-03** mission is significant because it is the **heaviest communication satellite** to be launched by India’s own launch vehicle, the **LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark 3)**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• This satellite is part of the **CMS series**, which is the successor to the long-running **GSAT** series. It is equipped with high-power **Ka-band** and **Ku-band** transponders to enhance data connectivity and **VSAT** services.
 
• The mission aims to achieve a lift-off mass exceeding previous indigenous records, pushing the payload capabilities of the **LVM3** rocket to its maximum potential for **Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO)** missions.
 
• The **CMS-03** is intended to provide expanded coverage for the **Indian mainland** as well as the **Andaman & Nicobar** and **Lakshadweep islands**, supporting the **Digital India** vision for high-speed internet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Private Space Payloads:** The first **private payload** launched from India was the **Vikram-S** sub-orbital rocket, developed by the startup **Skyroot Aerospace** under the **Prarambh** mission on **November 18, 2022**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Navigation Satellites:** India's first dedicated **navigation satellite** mission was the **IRNSS-1A**, which was launched on **July 1, 2013**, forming the basis of the **NavIC** (Navigation with Indian Constellation) system. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Mars Missions:** **India’s first Mars mission**, the **Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM)** or **Mangalyaan**, was launched on **November 5, 2013**, using the **PSLV-C25** rocket. It made **ISRO** the fourth space agency in the world to reach Mars. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **LVM3 Launch Vehicle:** Formerly known as **GSLV Mk III**, the **LVM3** is a three-stage heavy-lift launch vehicle. It consists of two **S200** solid rocket boosters, an **L110** liquid core stage, and a **C25** cryogenic upper stage, capable of carrying payloads up to **4,000 kg** to **GTO**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Frequency Bands:** The use of **Ka-band** in **CMS-03** allows for higher bandwidth and smaller ground station antennas compared to traditional **C-band** or **Ku-band** satellites.
 
• **Self-Reliance:** By launching such heavy satellites indigenously, India reduces its dependence on foreign agencies like the **European Space Agency (ESA)** or **SpaceX** for launching high-mass communication payloads.
 
• **Operational Life:** Like most **ISRO** communication satellites in **Geostationary Orbit**, the **CMS-03** is expected to have a mission life of over **10 to 12 years**, providing continuous service for broadcasting and secure government communications.

questions.question: Which apex agricultural research body is associated with the Indian Institute of Soil Science that organised World Soil Day celebrations in December 2025?

options.text: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Council of Agricultural Research**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Institute of Soil Science (IISS)** is a premier scientific institute for soil research, located in **Bhopal**, **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• It was established in **1988** under the aegis of the **Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)** to enhance the scientific basis of soil management.
 
• The **World Soil Day** celebrations, held on **5 December** annually, were organized by the institute in **December 2025** to emphasize the importance of soil health and sustainable resource management.
 
• The **Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)** is the apex body responsible for coordinating, guiding, and managing research and education in agriculture, including horticulture, fisheries, and animal sciences in **India**.
 
• The **IISS** plays a critical role in the **ICAR** network by focusing on nutrient management, soil fertility, and environmental impact assessments to ensure food security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR):**
 
 
• It was established on **16 July 1929** as a registered society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, following the report of the **Royal Commission on Agriculture**.
 
• Headquartered in **New Delhi**, it is one of the largest national agricultural systems in the world, reporting to the **Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE)** under the **Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare**.
 
• The **Union Minister of Agriculture** serves as the **President** of the **ICAR**.
 
 
 
• **World Soil Day:**
 
 
• The **International Union of Soil Sciences (IUSS)** recommended an international day to celebrate soil in **2002**.
 
• The **UN General Assembly** officially designated **5 December 2014** as the first official World Soil Day to honor the birthday of **H.M. King Bhumibol Adulyadej** of **Thailand**, who was a key proponent of this initiative.
 
• The primary objective is to focus attention on the importance of healthy soil and advocating for the sustainable management of soil resources.
 
 
 
• **Indian Institute of Soil Science (IISS):**
 
 
• The institute has developed various technologies like the **Mridaparikshak** (a digital soil test mini-lab) to assist farmers.
 
• It contributes significantly to the **Soil Health Card Scheme**, which was launched by the **Government of India** in **February 2015** to inform farmers about the nutrient status of their holdings.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Central Soil Salinity Research Institute (CSSRI):** Located in **Karnal**, **Haryana**, this institute focuses specifically on the reclamation and management of salt-affected soils.
 
• **Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR):** Established in **1942**, it is **India's** largest research and development organization, but it focuses on industrial and general science rather than being the apex body for **agricultural** research.
 
• **National Horticulture Board (NHB):** Established in **1984** by the **Government of India**, it focuses on the development of the high-tech horticulture industry and post-harvest management.
 
• **Soil Health and SDGs:** Sustainable soil management is vital for achieving the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly **Goal 2 (Zero Hunger)** and **Goal 15 (Life on Land)**.
</ul

questions.question: What was the Supreme Court's decision on April 28, 2025, regarding a new petition on the Waqf (Amendment) Act?

options.text: It accepted the petition for immediate hearing.
It referred the plea to the High Court.
It declined to entertain the fresh plea.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It declined to entertain the fresh plea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **April 28, 2025**, the **Supreme Court of India** took a significant stance regarding the legal challenges surrounding the **Waqf (Amendment) Act** by declining to entertain a fresh petition filed against the legislation.
 
• The bench, while presiding over the matter, observed that multiple petitions and deliberations regarding the **Waqf (Amendment) Act** were already in progress across various legal and legislative forums.
 
• The court noted that the **Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC)**, which was constituted to examine the nuances of the **Amendment Act**, was still in the process of finalizing its reports and recommendations.
 
• The **Supreme Court** emphasized that judicial intervention at this specific juncture might be premature given that the **Parliamentary** process for review and refinement of the act was not yet fully concluded. *Hence, the statement that it declined to entertain the fresh plea is correct.*
 
• The petitioners had sought a stay or a declaration of the act as **unconstitutional**, citing concerns over the autonomy of religious bodies, but the court maintained that the current legal framework allowed for the legislative review to take precedence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Waqf (Amendment) Act:**
 
 
• The **Waqf (Amendment) Act** was introduced to bring about sweeping reforms in the **Waqf Act of 1995**, primarily focusing on the **transparency**, **accountability**, and **digitization** of **Waqf properties** across **India**.
 
• One of the most debated features of the act includes the restructuring of the **State Waqf Boards** and the **Central Waqf Council** to include **women** and **non-Muslim members** in administrative roles.
 
• The act aims to streamline the process of **property registration** and prevent the encroachment of **Waqf land**, which is estimated to be over **6 lakh acres** across the country.
 
 
 
• **Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC):**
 
 
• The **JPC** is an ad-hoc committee of **Parliament** formed to examine specific bills or scandals; in this case, it was tasked with hearing stakeholders from different **Muslim organizations**, legal experts, and state governments.
 
• The committee's role is to ensure that the **Amendment Act** aligns with the **Constitution of India**, specifically **Article 25** and **Article 26**, which guarantee the right to manage religious affairs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Judicial Review and Policy:** The **Supreme Court** often practices **judicial restraint** when a legislative matter is under active consideration by a specialized **Parliamentary Committee** to avoid conflicting outcomes.
 
• **Waqf Board Authority:** Under the proposed amendments, the power of the **Waqf Board** to declare a property as "**Waqf by User**" has been a point of major legal contention, leading to numerous filings in **High Courts** and the **Apex Court**.
 
• **Date of Significance:** The decision on **April 28, 2025**, serves as a precedent that the **judiciary** will likely wait for the **final legislative version** of the act before passing a comprehensive judgment on its **constitutional validity**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following major wildlife surveys did the Indian Prime Minister announce to be conducted in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16th Asiatic Lion Population Estimation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** announced that the **16th Asiatic Lion Population Estimation** will be conducted in the year **2025** to assess the health and growth of the lion population in India.
 
• This estimation is a vital conservation exercise conducted every **five years** to monitor the world’s only wild population of **Asiatic Lions** (*Panthera leo leo*).
 
• The survey primarily covers the **Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary** along with the surrounding **Greater Gir** region in the **Saurashtra** landscape of **Gujarat**.
 
• The **15th Asiatic Lion Census** was originally due in **2020** but was replaced by a restricted exercise called **"Poonam Avlokan"** due to the **COVID-19** pandemic, which recorded **674** lions.
 
• The **2025** survey will utilize advanced technology, including **GPS** tracking, **camera traps**, and **individual identification markers**, to ensure a more scientific and accurate headcount.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Project Lion**:
 
 
• Launched on **August 15, 2020**, **Project Lion** aims at the **holistic conservation** of the Asiatic Lion and its landscape.
 
• It focuses on **habitat development**, engaging **modern technologies** in lion management, and addressing **human-wildlife conflict**.
 
• The project also envisages the **relocation** of some lions to different sites within **Gujarat** or other states like **Madhya Pradesh** (Kuno) to prevent extinction from disease.
 
 
 
• **Asiatic Lion Characteristics**:
 
 
• The **Asiatic Lion** is slightly smaller than the **African Lion** and possesses a distinctive **longitudinal fold of skin** running along its belly.
 
• It is listed as **Endangered** on the **IUCN Red List** and is protected under **Schedule I** of the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**.
 
 
 
• **Population Trends**:
 
 
• Between **2015** and **2020**, the population showed a significant growth of **29%**, increasing from **523** to **674** individuals.
 
• The distribution area of the lions has expanded from **22,000 sq. km** in **2015** to about **30,000 sq. km** in **2020**, covering districts like **Junagadh**, **Gir Somnath**, **Amreli**, and **Bhavnagar**.
 
 
 
• **Poonam Avlokan**:
 
 
• This was an alternative estimation method conducted on **full moon nights** where forest guards observed lions from their respective beats.
 
• While not as exhaustive as a full census, it provides critical interim **data** on **demographics** and **geographical distribution**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Gujarat Forest Department** is the nodal agency responsible for organizing and executing these **wildlife surveys**.
 
• The **Lion’s status** as a **flagship species** makes the **2025** survey a priority for international **biodiversity** conservationists.
 
• Efforts are being made to establish **Barda Wildlife Sanctuary** as a second home for lions to reduce the density in **Gir** and mitigate risks of **epidemics**.

questions.question: As part of Tripura’s tech-driven disaster preparedness initiative launched in August 2025, how many automated weather stations and rain gauges are proposed to be installed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**26**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **August 2025**, the **Government of Tripura** launched a comprehensive **tech-driven disaster preparedness initiative** aimed at mitigating the impact of natural calamities through advanced monitoring.
 
• As part of this initiative, the state has proposed the installation of **26 automated weather stations (AWS)** and **automated rain gauges** to facilitate **real-time data collection** and analysis.
 
• These high-tech installations are designed to provide precise **meteorological data**, which is critical for the state's **Early Warning System (EWS)**, especially during the **monsoon season**.
 
• The primary goal of deploying these **26** units is to enhance the accuracy of weather forecasts at a **micro-level**, allowing **disaster management** teams to respond more effectively to threats like **flash floods**, **landslides**, and **cyclonic storms**.
 
• The initiative integrates **Information and Communication Technology (ICT)** with traditional **disaster management** protocols to ensure that information reaches the **last mile** in a timely manner.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Vulnerability of Tripura:** 
 
 
• **Tripura** is situated in the **northeastern part** of **India** and is highly susceptible to hydro-meteorological disasters due to its hilly terrain and high **annual rainfall**.
 
• The state also falls under **Seismic Zone V**, making it one of the most **earthquake-prone** regions in the country.
 
 
 
• **Function of Automated Weather Stations:**
 
 
• An **Automated Weather Station (AWS)** measures various parameters such as **temperature**, **humidity**, **wind speed**, **wind direction**, and **solar radiation** without manual intervention.
 
• The data is typically transmitted via **GPRS** or **Satellite communication** to a central server at the **State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA)**.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Agriculture:**
 
 
• The installation of these **26** stations will significantly benefit the **farming community** by providing localized weather alerts, helping them protect **crops** from sudden **heavy rainfall** or **hailstorms**.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Coverage:**
 
 
• The project ensures coverage across all **8 districts** of **Tripura**, including **West Tripura**, **South Tripura**, **Dhalai**, and **North Tripura**, creating a robust network of **environmental sensors**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Modernization of Disaster Response:** The **August 2025** project marks a significant shift from **reactive** to **proactive** disaster management, utilizing **predictive modeling** based on the data from the **26** new stations.
 
• **Collaboration:** This initiative is often carried out in coordination with the **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** and the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** to align with **national standards** of safety and **data accuracy**.
 
• **Number of Units:** The specific count of **26** was determined based on a **gap analysis** of the existing **meteorological infrastructure** in the state to ensure no region remains unmonitored.
 
• **Digital Tripura:** This move is a subset of the broader **"Digital Tripura"** vision, which seeks to use **technology** for **governance** and **public safety**.
</ul

questions.question: According to the 2025 Sustainable Development Report, what is India’s Spillover Score?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**96.07**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **2025 Sustainable Development Report (SDR)**, India has achieved a **Spillover Score** of **96.07**.
 
• The **Spillover Index** measures the extent to which a country's domestic actions and consumption patterns create positive or negative **externalities** (impacts) on other countries' ability to achieve the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• A higher score on the **Spillover Index** (closer to **100**) indicates that a country causes fewer negative **transboundary impacts**; India's score of **96.07** suggests it has relatively low negative impacts on other nations compared to many developed economies.
 
• The report is published annually by the **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**, which has been working under the auspices of the **UN Secretary-General** since **2012**.
 
• The **2025 report** assesses all **193 UN Member States**, providing a comprehensive overview of global progress toward the **2030 Agenda**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Components of Spillover Score**: The index tracks three main categories: **Environmental & Social spillovers** embodied in trade (e.g., carbon emissions or child labor in supply chains), **Economy & Finance spillovers** (e.g., unfair tax competition), and **Security spillovers** (e.g., arms exports).
 
• **The SDG Index vs. Spillover Index**: While the **SDG Index** measures a country’s internal progress toward the **17 goals**, the **Spillover Index** specifically looks at international consequences. Often, high-income countries rank high on the SDG Index but very low on the Spillover Index due to heavy consumption.
 
• **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**: Led by renowned economist **Professor Jeffrey Sachs**, the SDSN mobilizes scientific and technical expertise from academia, civil society, and the private sector.
 
• **India's SDG Journey**: India has integrated the SDGs into its national development strategy through the **NITI Aayog**, focusing on major schemes like **Jal Jeevan Mission** and **Ayushman Bharat** to address domestic targets while maintaining a stable international footprint.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Context**: The **2025 Report** emphasizes the urgent need for a "**Global Financial Architecture**" reform to support developing nations in closing the financing gap required to meet **2030 targets**.
 
• **Data and Fact**: In the **2025** assessment, countries with scores above **95** on the spillover index are generally considered to be "exporting" very few negative environmental or social costs to the rest of the world.
 
• **Yearly Comparison**: India's **Spillover Score** has remained consistently high over the last few years, reflecting its status as a country that, while developing, does not disproportionately burden the global environment through its **trade-linked consumption**.
 
• **Target 2030**: The **Sustainable Development Goals** were adopted by all **United Nations** Member States in **2015** as a universal call to action to end poverty and protect the planet by the **year 2030**.

questions.question: Which organisation announced plans to develop a new indicator for measuring extreme poverty in India in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**World Bank**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Bank** has announced its plans to develop and introduce a **new indicator** for measuring **extreme poverty** in **India** and other nations in **2025**.
 
• This initiative is part of a broader effort to update the **international poverty lines** to reflect the changing **economic realities** and **price levels** globally, moving away from the **2017 Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** benchmarks.
 
• Currently, the **World Bank** uses a threshold of **$2.15 per person per day** to define **extreme poverty**, but for a **lower-middle-income** country like **India**, there is a growing need for indicators that better capture the **cost of living** and **basic needs**.
 
• The **2025** revision aims to provide a more accurate assessment of **poverty trends**, which is crucial for tracking **Sustainable Development Goal 1 (SDG 1)**, which targets the eradication of **extreme poverty** for all people everywhere.
 
• By refining these metrics, the **World Bank** intends to help **policymakers** in **India** better identify **vulnerable populations** and design more effective **social security** and **poverty alleviation** programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The World Bank**:
 
 
• It is an **international financial institution** established in **1944** at the **Bretton Woods Conference**.
 
• Headquartered in **Washington, D.C.**, it provides **loans** and **grants** to the governments of **low-income** and **middle-income** countries for the purpose of pursuing **capital projects**.
 
• The current **President** of the World Bank is **Ajay Banga**, who assumed office in **June 2023**.
 
 
 
• **Poverty Lines by Income Group**:
 
 
• The **World Bank** maintains different poverty lines based on a country's **economic status**: **$2.15** for **low-income**, **$3.65** for **lower-middle-income**, and **$6.85** for **upper-middle-income** countries.
 
• As **India** is classified as a **lower-middle-income** economy, the **$3.65** line is often considered more relevant for its **domestic policy** context than the **extreme poverty** line of **$2.15**.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog and Poverty (Option 1)**:
 
 
• In **India**, **NITI Aayog** is the nodal agency for monitoring **poverty**. It released the **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**, which uses **12 indicators** across **health**, **education**, and **standard of living**.
 
• According to **NITI Aayog's** reports, **India** has seen a significant decline in **multidimensional poverty**, with millions escaping poverty between **2013-14** and **2022-23**.
 
 
 
• **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)**:
 
 
• This is an **economic theory** and **metric** used to compare **economic productivity** and **standards of living** between countries by adjusting for **price level differences**.
 
• The **World Bank** updates its poverty lines whenever new **International Comparison Program (ICP)** data on **PPPs** become available to ensure the **real value** of the poverty line remains constant over time.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context**: The **International Poverty Line** was first introduced as **$1 a day** in **1990** based on **1985** prices. It was subsequently revised to **$1.08**, **$1.25**, **$1.90**, and finally to the current **$2.15** in **September 2022**.
 
• **Global Poverty Goal**: The **World Bank** aims to reduce the share of the **global population** living in **extreme poverty** to less than **3%** by the **year 2030**.
 
• **India's Role**: Since **India** represents a significant portion of the **global population**, any change in how **poverty** is measured in **India** has a massive impact on **global poverty statistics** and **World Bank** projections.
 
• **Data Sources**: For **India**, the **World Bank** often relies on the **Consumer Expenditure Survey (CES)** conducted by the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**.

questions.question: Which organisation developed Delhi's first Centre of Excellence for Sports in Dwarka's Sector 8, inaugurated in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi Development Authority (DDA)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Delhi Development Authority (DDA)** has developed the city's first dedicated **Centre of Excellence (CoE) for Sports** located in **Sector 8, Dwarka**.
 
• The facility was officially inaugurated in **May 2025**, marking a significant milestone in the urban sports infrastructure of the **National Capital Territory of Delhi**.
 
• Unlike traditional sports complexes, this **Centre of Excellence** is specifically designed to provide high-performance training environments for athletes focusing on **Olympic sports** such as **Archery**, **Athletics**, and **Football**.
 
• The project is part of **DDA’s** broader mission to transform **Dwarka** into a major sports hub, supplementing existing facilities and providing a platform for professional coaching and scientific sports management.
 
• The **DDA** serves as the primary agency for land and infrastructure development in Delhi under the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs**, **Government of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Infrastructure Features:**
 
 
• The **Dwarka Sector 8** complex boasts **world-class facilities**, including a **synthetic athletic track**, specialized **Archery grounds**, and international-standard **Football pitches**.
 
• It also includes **hostel facilities** for resident athletes, ensuring that talented youth from across the country can train in **Delhi** under professional supervision.
 
 
 
• **Role of the DDA in Sports:**
 
 
• The **Delhi Development Authority** currently maintains over **15 sports complexes**, **3 mini-sports complexes**, and **2 public golf courses** (including the **Qutab Golf Course** and **Bhalswa Golf Course**).
 
• The transition toward "Centres of Excellence" indicates a shift from providing general recreational facilities to fostering **competitive excellence** in alignment with the **Master Plan for Delhi (MPD) 2041**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Organizations:**
 
 
• While the **Sports Authority of India (SAI)** manages national-level training programs (like the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme - TOPS**), the **DDA** is the local authority responsible for the physical construction and maintenance of these specific assets in Delhi.
 
• The **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)** acts as the governing body for Olympic movements but does not typically undertake large-scale civil construction projects like the **Dwarka CoE**.
 
 
 
• **Socio-Economic Impact:**
 
 
• The establishment of such centers in **Dwarka** helps in the decentralization of sports facilities, which were previously concentrated in **South Delhi** (e.g., **Siri Fort**) and **East Delhi** (e.g., **Yamuna Sports Complex**).
 
• It supports the **Khelo India** initiative by providing the necessary hardware (infrastructure) to complement the software (talent scouting and training).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Lieutenant Governor of Delhi**, who serves as the **Chairman of the DDA**, has been a key proponent of the timely completion of the **Dwarka sports projects**.
 
• The **Centre of Excellence** model aims to bridge the gap between amateur play and professional sports by integrating **sports science**, **physiotherapy**, and **nutrition** within the same premises.
 
• Recent developments in **2024-2025** have seen **DDA** increasing its budget allocation for **green spaces** and **multi-utility sports arenas** to cater to the growing population of the sub-city of **Dwarka**.
